# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

# [tinydb] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:e6c2e3098d2d⟧
Mode: Code Development (code)

Legend: 🎯session ●bugfix ◆feature ↻refactor ✓change ○discovery ⚖decision ⚠security_alert ⚷security_note ⊘sensitive
Format: ID TIME TYPE TITLE
Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 11 obs (5,163t read) | 38,808t work | 87% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
1 10:51a ○ JSONStorage keeps a long-lived file handle opened in access_mode
2 " ○ JSONStorage.write() overwrites the file in place without atomic replacement
3 " ◆ JSONStorage writes now go through a temp file and atomic rename
4 " ○ Full tinydb test suite passes with the atomic JSONStorage write
5 " ◆ Regression test added for atomic JSONStorage write failure
S2 Make tinydb JSONStorage writes crash-safe so a process dying mid-write cannot leave a truncated db.json. A service's db.json was truncated after an OOM kill during a write. (Nov 3, 10:52 AM)
S1 Make tinydb JSONStorage writes crash-safe so a process dying mid-write cannot leave a truncated db.json, after an OOM kill truncated a service's database file. (Nov 3, 10:52 AM)
6 10:52a ✓ Atomic JSONStorage write and its regression test were reverted from the working tree
7 10:55a ◆ JSONStorage gains a journal-based crash-safe write mode
8 " ○ Journal crash-recovery tests appended; suite shows 1 failure and 69 errors in json-backed tests
9 " ● Root cause of json-backed TypeErrors found: JSONStorage journal path concatenation fails on PosixPath
10 10:56a ● PosixPath journal fix restores suite to 233 passing; one crash-injection test still fails
11 " ● Crash-injection test fixed by truncating torn file; full suite passes at 234 tests
S3 Make tinydb JSONStorage writes crash-safe after an OOM kill truncated db.json. A process dying mid-write should leave a readable database on the next open, either the old or the new state. Add tests. (Nov 3, 10:56 AM)
**Investigated**: The session read tinydb/storages.py in full and checked the git working tree, which was clean at the start. The earlier temp-file-and-rename approach was reverted because db.json is a single-file bind mount and rename fails with EBUSY. The session then tried a journal-based approach and ran the full test suite several times.

**Learned**: JSONStorage overwrites db.json in place, so a crash mid-write leaves a truncated file. A single-file bind mount rules out replacing the inode. The repo's pytest.ini coverage options fail in this environment, so tests run with `-c /dev/null --rootdir=. tests`. Passing a pathlib.Path to JSONStorage broke the journal path, because `path + '.journal'` raises TypeError on PosixPath. Wrapping the path in os.fspath fixes it. A simulated torn write only produces an unparseable file if the handle is truncated after the partial write.

**Completed**: JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py gained an opt-in `journal=True` parameter. Before the in-place write, the full new state is written and fsynced to `<path>.journal`, along with the directory. On open in writable modes, a complete journal is replayed onto db.json and a torn journal is discarded. The journal is removed after a successful write. Six crash-recovery tests were added to tests/test_storages.py. The full suite passes with 234 tests, which is the original 228 plus 6 new ones. Changes are uncommitted, with tinydb/storages.py and tests/test_storages.py modified.

**Next Steps**: Confirm with ops where the journal file can live. A journal beside db.json in a bind-mounted container is lost if the container is recreated. Options under consideration include a persistent directory and a `journal_path` parameter. The production db.json still needs restoring from backup, which is outside this repo.

**Notes**: The crash-recovery tests simulate torn writes by injecting a partial write and a truncate. They do not test a real process kill. Journal recovery is not atomic in-place overwrite, and it depends on the journal being intact. If the directory is not writable, write() now raises where it previously succeeded, so callers in that environment need journal=False.
